issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath §6.2 comparison semantics / DuckDB native-vs-fallback parity
issues.evidence: Native C++ and forced Python fallback both return an empty result for valid expressions with incompatible operands, but fhirpath_is_valid disagrees. Probes on 2026-05-17: native SELECT fhirpath('{}'::JSON, '''10'' > 2'), fhirpath_is_valid('''10'' > 2') returned ([], true), while forced Python fallback returned ([], false). The same drift reproduced for '''x'' + 1' and 'true < 1'. The Python fallback path in fhir4ds/fhirpath/duckdb/udf.py:587-595 compiles and evaluates against a sample Patient resource, then catches every exception and returns false, so semantic empty-result errors from sample evaluation are conflated with invalid expressions.
issues.root_cause: Python fallback validation uses sample evaluation as a validity oracle and treats FHIRPathError from valid-but-empty comparison/arithmetic expressions as invalid, while native validation treats those expressions as valid because evaluation returns an empty collection without throwing.
issues.resolution: Fixed Python fallback fhirpath_is_valid() so valid comparison/arithmetic expressions that evaluate to empty are treated as expression-valid, while unresolved type specifiers, wrong type-function arity, and malformed temporal literals remain invalid. Added native-vs-forced-fallback regression coverage.
